nodes.label: fetchpriority is the positive authorial LCP claim; loading="eager" is not
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - t9-lcp-preload-contract [ses_f1696bb14ffeRoKS2rSP804CT3].md:L8237] The task's suggested rule was too broad, and I narrowed it.** The brief says a route with an `` using "eager loading **or** a `fetchpriority`" must have a preload. Eager alone is not an LCP claim: `lp/campaign.astro:66` has `loading="eager"` on a 28x28 logo, and its LCP is the h1. A preload there is the exact harm the rescoping was meant to prevent. I keyed the rule on `fetchpriority` and pinned the reason with a dedicated test, so the exclusion is deliberate and documented rather than accidental. This also means a future hero that gets `loading="eager"` but forgets `fetchpriority` will not be caught. I think that is the right trade, since `fetchpriority` is a positive authorial claim, but it is a real gap.
nodes.norm_label: fetchpriority is the positive lcp claim

nodes.label: googlevideo URL expiry, IP binding and signature
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7796] **The real authorisation is in the signed URL, and it is IP-bound, not header-bound.** Live signed URLs embed the client IP in both query and path form: `…&ip=83.34.78.41&…` ([yt-dlp #16007](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16007)), and path form `…/expire/1768903243/ei/…/ip/59.11.11.11/requiressl/yes/…` ([yt-dlp #15634](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15634)). The `sparams` signed-parameter set is `expire,ei,ip,id,itag,source,requiressl,xpc,gcr,siu,bui,spc,vprv,svpuc,mime,ns,rqh,gir,clen,dur,lmt` — **no `referer`**

nodes.label: WebKitGTK disables HLS by default and gates MP4/AAC on installed GStreamer plugins
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7803] **HLS is disabled by default in WebKitGTK.** WebKitGTK 2.38.4 release notes: *"**Disable HLS media playback by default**, which makes web sites use MSE instead. If needed `WEBKIT_GST_ENABLE_HLS_SUPPORT=1` can be set in the environment to enable it back."* (<https://webkitgtk.org/2023/02/02/webkitgtk2.38.4-released.html>). Since Tauri v2's Linux webview is WebKitGTK, **the `web_safari` HLS escape hatch is not available to you without an env var, and even then native HLS in `<audio>` is unsupported** (WebKit has no native HLS audio path; it needs MSE + hls.js).

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r2-rust-integration-options [ses_f24bc733bffeiT4rZVT2IvsOtn].md:L7804] WebKitGTK's MP4/AAC support is gated on installed GStreamer plugins (`gst-plugins-libav` et al.) — WebKit bug [#135972 "[GStreamer] unrelated codecs required to play videos"](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=135972) documents that removing `gst-plugins-libav` breaks `video/mp4`, and that WebKit gates the mime type on `gstRegistryHasDecoder("video/x-h264")`. **H** for the dependency existing, **UNVERIFIED** for any specific user distro. **Always prefer `audio/webm; codecs="opus"` (itag 251) over `audio/mp4; codecs="mp4a.40.2"` (itag 140) on Linux.** You can check at runtime with `document.createElement('audio').canPlayType(...)` before committing.
nodes.norm_label: webkitgtk hls disabled and codecs gated by gstreamer
